messages:
alex: Hey team — noticing intermittent failures in the eval harness artifact upload. Runner logs show `checksum mismatch` for some multipart uploads to our trace bucket.

maria: Ugh, saw that too this morning on the quantized-runner job. Any consistent pattern on which traces fail? large ones? many small parts?

alex: Mostly larger traces (>12MB). The runner retries and eventually uploads, but the manifest ETAG doesn't match and S3 rejects the assembly.

jong: Can you paste the failing log snippet?

alex: Sure — from runner stdout: 
```
[2026-02-12T09:15:02Z] INFO upload part 3 size=5242880 md5=3b7a...
[2026-02-12T09:15:03Z] ERROR multipart complete failed: InvalidETag: ETag does not match computed

request id: 8F4A...
```

kevin: That looks like either part-ordering mismatch or we're not sending Content-MD5 for parts. S3 computes the final ETag from parts. If any part is corrupted or order differs, complete fails.

maria: Runner uses concurrent part uploads with a simple map of indices -> parts. There was a recent change to the goroutine pool to improve throughput — could be a race in indexing.

jong: Another possibility: gzip step pre- or post-parting. If we compress then chunk, but the code recomputes md5 on the uncompressed buffer by mistake, ETag won't line up.

alex: Repro command I used locally: 
```bash
python -m eval_runner.run --trace-dir ./tmp/traces --upload-bucket redwood-eval-traces-staging --multipart-threshold 5MB
```
Gives deterministic fail on one sample when I toggle `--concurrency 8`.

ci-bot: CI flake detected: pipeline eval-harness-upload (job 2379) failed 2/10 runs with multipart InvalidETag.

kevin: We should add a small unit that simulates out-of-order part index submissions and verify manifest assembly picks index not arrival order.

maria: Agreed. Also noticed storage service TTL for temp objects is 24h and a retention sweep sometimes deletes a 'tmp-' key mid-upload if parts uploaded under temp prefix. Might produce partial manifests that confuse completion.

storage-bot: Alert: delete-sweep removed 17 objects with prefix "tmp-upload-1824" at 2026-02-12T08:40:00Z per retention policy.

jong: If the sweep deletes temp parts before complete, that would definitely lead to checksum errors. We should ensure temp prefix is protected while an upload session is active (heartbeat).

alex: Proposed action items: 1) Add Content-MD5 headers for each multipart part upload; 2) Harden runner indexing to use explicit partNumber on complete; 3) Prevent retention sweep on tmp keys with active session heartbeat; 4) Add CI test that runs concurrent-part uploads + simulated retention deletion to reproduce.

kevin: I'll own (1) + (2). Will add a small test that flips concurrency and asserts S3 complete success.

maria: I'll modify retention service to check for an active session tag (x-eval-session) before deleting tmp keys. Add TTL extension on heartbeat.

jong: I'll wire the CI test into the eval-harness pipeline and add flaky alert suppression until we fix. Also add a synthetic large-trace test to nightly to catch regressions.

alex: Thanks. One more note — let's also emit a clear metric in metrics-api for `trace_upload_checksum_failures` so we can alert if rate > 0.5% over a day.

kevin: Good call. I'll add a counter and tag by runner version.

maria: I'll document the tmp-key heartbeat contract in the storage README and update agents so DS teams don't rely on deleted tmp artifacts.

alex: Cool. I'll push a small repro branch with logs and the exact failing sample id (sample_20260212_8472) so you can run locally.

ci-bot: CI pipeline triggered for branch fix/multipart-md5 by kevin.

storage-bot: Retention sweep paused on prefix tmp-upload-1824 pending investigation.

alex: Thanks all — will follow up with PR links and the failing sample dump in the thread. :thumbsup:
